items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: poor George Buck has got 150 trillion new masters, which he's just purchased, and I don't know when he's going to get to put them all out.

ctx.x: Dick Allen or Johnny Wiggs. You tell them, Dick. I believe that that George Buck has bought the rights to

that nana. It's Johnny's record. I don't know what to do. You can write to him in Columbia, South Carolina. It will be out, but when, I don't know, poor George Buck has got 150 trillion new masters, which he's just purchased, and I don't know when he's going to get to put them all out. So the best way to do is to try to get to dig it out of some record shop. Just continue. There's an awful fine record man. You tell me his name. He has his record shop on Royal right near Canal Joe. I can't remember the man's name.…

over. We'll be back right after this. This is WTIS on the subject of New Orleans jazz, a subject we certainly should have presented before now, but I can assure you that we will do this again and again, especially since those phones are ringing like they are. The line, when they become available, available, 523-2404. The present time in downtown New Orleans, we have partly cloudy skies with a temperature of 60 WTIX degrees.
